headline: Cohere, the Canadian AI company, said it plans to buy Aisle, a Prague-based startup whose AI finds security flaws in software.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a clear acquisition in AI security, but only a letter of intent with no price.
importance_line: Matters to companies and open-source maintainers who rely on code being checked for flaws and to Cohere's push into security; it is only a letter of intent, with no price, and Aisle's performance claims are its own.
summary: The Globe and Mail reports that Toronto-based Cohere signed a letter of intent, an early agreement to proceed, to acquire Aisle, a Prague startup founded in 2024 whose AI systems find and help fix software flaws; terms were not disclosed. Aisle says its systems turned up more than 500 previously unknown flaws across over 100 code bases over the past 12 months, and Cohere plans a substantial investment to make Prague its hub for AI cybersecurity.
notes: Investing.com (Reuters copy) blocked; credited to The Globe and Mail, which reported its own story.
